### Solution Steps:

1. **Given Data:**
   - Line $AB = 85\text{ mm}$, parallel to HP, inclined at $30^\circ$ to VP.
   - End A: $20\text{ mm}$ above HP, $40\text{ mm}$ in front of VP.

2. **Projections:**
   - Draw the reference line $XY$.
   - Mark the front view of end $A'$ at $20\text{ mm}$ above $XY$, and the top view of end $A$ at $40\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.
   - Since the line is parallel to HP, its front view $A'B'$ is parallel to $XY$.
   - Since the line is inclined at $30^\circ$ to VP, draw the top view $ab$ of length $85\text{ mm}$ inclined at $30^\circ$ to the $XY$ line starting from $a$.
   - Project $B'$ upward from $b$ onto the horizontal projector passing through $A'$ to complete the front view $A'B'$ of length $85\text{ mm}$.

3. **Traces of the Line:**
   - **Vertical Trace (VT):** Since the line is parallel to HP, it will never intersect the HP, hence **no HT** exists.
   - To find the VT, extend the top view $ab$ until it intersects the $XY$ line (or extend the front view $A'B'$ to meet the $XY$ line if needed). Here, since $AB$ is parallel to HP and inclined to VP, extend the top view $ab$ to meet $XY$ at point $x$. Project a perpendicular down/up to find the VT on the front view extension.
proTip: A line parallel to one reference plane has no trace on that plane (e.g., parallel to HP means no horizontal trace).
